title: Request routing & retention lab demo - Krypton Warehousing
summary: Console + API walkthrough focusing on request storage toggles, redaction, and routing policies. Customer wants VPC/private options and an ability to turn off request storage per route. Discussed trade-offs for latency vs dedupe/caching and next steps: share SOC2 + architecture doc, pricing, and lab pilot setup.
next_steps: Share proposed pilot SOW and pricing (AE)
Provision lab tenancy and sample dataset for benchmark (SE)
Follow up meeting to kick off pilot week of 2028-03-12

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samira Patel (Redwood CSM); Olivia Park (CTO, Krypton), Daniel Ortiz (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Compliance), Marco Ruiz (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick demo of console toggles, showed request-storage switch, redaction profiles, and routing policies. Questions about EU data residency and dedicated capacity.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Ethan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer and Samira from customer success. How are we doing in london... sorry, I mean in, uh, across the group?
[00:10] Olivia Park: Good, thanks. We're in Chicago and Madrid, a mix. Priya here is in Dublin so timezone fun.
[00:16] Daniel Ortiz: Hi. We'll keep this focused on retention controls and routing, primarily. We're trying to figure out if we can keep request storage off for PII-heavy routes but keep high-performance caching for other flows.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll demo. Today we'll toggle the request-storage per-route on the Console, show redaction profiles for PII, then cover routing policy rules that can send traffic to dedicated capacity or hosted fallback.
[00:45] Speaker 1: quick note that some of the names in the slide were truncated, sorry.
[00:50] Maya Chen: No worries. So first, Console view — I'm in the routes tab. Here's our production route, "order-ocr", and you can see the request-storage toggle here. For PII-heavy routes you can set it to "ephemeral" which means we don't persist request payloads beyond KV cache lifetime, or set to "retain with redaction" which runs our redact pipeline and stores sanitized transcripts.
[01:15] Marco Ruiz: Is ephemeral truly zero storage? We still need logs for debugging sometimes.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Good question. Ephemeral mode keeps only in-memory KV cache for the duration of the request and short tail tokens for session semantics, then evicts. We do keep telemetry metrics and aggregated token counts, but not the raw prompt/response. Debug logs for a particular session require enabling a temporary storage flag or a snapshot export which is auditable.
[01:42] Priya Nair: That sounds okay, but we need auditability — SOC 2 and possibility to pull raw logs for a legal hold if required, under controlled access.
[01:51] Samira Patel: Yes, access controls are RBACed and all exports are logged. We'll share the SOC 2 docs after the call.
[01:58] Olivia Park: Also we need EU residency for data at rest. Our billing and some logs are in the US, but EEA request content must stay in eu nodes.
[02:08] Maya Chen: We support region pinning per-route. You can create a policy that routes "eu-*" prefixes to eu-dedicated region. If capacity isn't available we can failover to a compatible model in a different region but only if you allow cross-border fallback — otherwise the request errors.
[02:25] Daniel Ortiz: What's the fallback behavior latency-wise? If we route to dedicated and it's cold, do we see long tail 2–3 second stalls?
[02:33] Maya Chen: There are a couple of knobs: keep-warm policies and burst capacity. With a warm pool your p95 for token generation remains low; cold-starts add overhead. We also showed Optimize suggestions that recommend batching windows and quantization settings to balance latency/cost.
[02:50] Ethan Brooks: To add, we can do canary routing: 90% to dedicated, 10% to hosted, so you get safety nets without disrupting SLAs.
[02:58] Marco Ruiz: Are redaction rules customizable? We have custom SKU numbers and some customer IDs that look like phone numbers.
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we have pre-built profiles (PII: SSN, email, phone), plus regex-based custom redactors you can upload via the API or Console. There is a small performance hit for heavy regex pipelines but for typical forms it's negligible.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Can we have per-field redaction that replaces values with stable pseudonyms so downstream features can link sessions without exposing PII?
[03:29] Maya Chen: Yes — we showed "stable-hash" substitution in the redaction profile, which gives deterministic pseudonyms. It writes a mapping to an encrypted index if you enable it — that's KMS-backed. The mapping can also be stored in your own KMS if you run Redwood Private.
[03:45] Olivia Park: On Private: we'd likely want Private (VPC) or an on-prem package for compliance. What's the install footprint?
[03:52] Ethan Brooks: For Private, there's a control plane managed by us, with a customer-managed VPC for data plane. Typical install for the compute nodes is a few GPU instances; we'll share our install sizing guide.
[04:02] Daniel Ortiz: Can you demo the API flag for retention? We might want to flip it dynamically per request.
[04:08] Maya Chen: Absolutely — here's a quick curl example (pasted):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \ 
  -d '{"route":"order-ocr","input":"...","meta":{"retain_request":false,"redaction_profile":"ephemeral"}}'
[04:30] Maya Chen: Note retain_request:false disables storage for that particular call, regardless of route default. It's useful for ad-hoc operations.
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: Nice. If we set retain_request:true but redaction_profile to "mask-emails-only" do you still store the masked content?
[04:44] Maya Chen: Yes, store sanitized content. We also store a checksum of raw input for dedupe detection but the checksum is a one-way salted hash and not reversible unless you have the original payload.
[04:55] Speaker 2: some background noise, apologies.
[04:58] Maya Chen: No problem. Next, i'll show routing policy rules — here's a rule that matches route prefix "order-*" and uses a weighted policy to send 80% to dedicated-prod-eu and 20% to hosted-fallback. You can add constraints like "only if token-length < 1024" or "only outside business hours".
[05:20] Daniel Ortiz: The "token-length" constraint — is that measured pre-encode or post-tokenize?
[05:26] Maya Chen: It's post-tokenize. The runtime reports token estimates and the policy engine evaluates the condition before enqueueing.
[05:33] Priya Nair: For audit, does the routing decision get logged with the request? We need to tie decisions back to events for compliance reporting.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes, routing metadata is emitted as part of telemetry and persisted for X days depending on your retention policy. If you have ephemerality on, we only keep routing metadata and aggregated metrics not the payload.
[05:52] Olivia Park: What about function/tool calling and structured outputs? Any extra exposure risk?
[05:58] Maya Chen: Function calls are treated as part of the response pipeline. You can instruct the runtime to not persist tool call arguments via the same retain_request flag. Structured outputs can be redacted field-by-field.
[06:12] Ethan Brooks: Switching gears — Optimize suggestions. We ran a quick scan on your sample shapes and it recommends a quantized model for mid-length orders and a slightly larger context window for OCR batches. That gives a 25% cost reduction in our simulation.
[06:28] Daniel Ortiz: Can you share the Optimize report and the benchmark spreadsheet?
[06:31] Ethan Brooks: Yes we'll share the Optimize export and a benchmark template. Maya will provision a lab and run a 2-hour ingest with your sample logs so we can feed real telemetry.
[06:42] Marco Ruiz: One concern — does the redaction pipeline ever alter semantics that downstream ML depends on? For example removing punctuation or normalizing dates?
[06:50] Maya Chen: The redaction pipeline is configurable. By default it's conservative — we only replace sensitive tokens and preserve surrounding context. There's also a "normalize" mode for heavy anonymization which can change semantics. We recommend running evals on a holdout set before rolling that out.
[07:06] Priya Nair: About legal hold — you mentioned exports are auditable. If a subpoena comes, what's the process?
[07:12] Samira Patel: We have a documented process in our legal + compliance playbook. Exports are gated to admins, require justification, and are logged. We'll include that playbook in the security bundle.
[07:22] Olivia Park: Pricing question — if we use ephemeral mode for 70% of traffic and retain for 30% for analytics, how does billing work? Per-token still?
[07:30] Ethan Brooks: Billing is still per-token for generation and per-embedding units when applicable. There's a small storage charge for retained payloads and a per-GB charge for redaction storage. We'll provide a sample cost model based on your mix.
[07:42] Daniel Ortiz: Could we schedule a 1-week pilot with 1M tokens/day to stress the routing and redaction?
[07:48] Maya Chen: We can. For that scale we'd recommend Dedicated reserved pool for predictability; we can scope a short-term burst capacity if you want to try hosted first.
[07:58] Olivia Park: Let's plan the pilot. We'll send anonymized logs. Also want to see failure modes: what happens when the redaction pipeline times out?
[08:07] Maya Chen: If redaction times out we can configure automatic fallback: either reject the request, queue for async redaction, or forward raw to a quarantined mailbox if you opt in. Defaults are conservative and favor rejection to avoid inadvertent exposure.
[08:22] Priya Nair: Ok that's important. Also need proof that the KMS integration means we control keys — we want BYOK for pseudonym maps.
[08:31] Ethan Brooks: BYOK supported in Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption where keys can be customer-managed in several clouds. We'll add a section about that in the security bundle.
[08:42] Speaker 3: someone typing, background.
[08:45] Ethan Brooks: Alright quick recap and next steps — we'll send SOC2 + architecture and the Optimize report, Maya will provision the lab tenant and run ingestion with the sample logs, and we'll target pilot kickoff week of 2028-03-12. Any other blockers?
[09:00] Daniel Ortiz: None from platform, just need the SOW and cost examples.
[09:04] Olivia Park: Compliance will review security bundle, and Priya will follow up with specific redaction policy asks.
[09:10] Ethan Brooks: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the attachments and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[09:17] Call ends.

Notes about transcription: Some proper nouns mis-heard (e.g., "ephemeral" transcribed consistently but sometimes shows as "effemeral" in slides), and there were a couple short audio dropouts around 04:55 and 08:42.
